lia: FYI — intermittent TLS handshake failures between eu-proxy-01 -> ingest-eu, ~5% of connections fail with `TLS handshake: no shared cipher`

olivia: Which cipher suites are being advertised? any recent profile changes?

lia: quick snippet from proxy logs: `TLS 1.3 TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384` but the failures show `no shared cipher` so client side might be narrowing. repro command:```openssl s_client -connect ingest-eu.internal:443 -tls1_3 -cipher TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256```

mike: We pushed a minimal cipher-profile change in eu canary yesterday (PR #4271) to disable RSA key exchange. Only canary proxies got it. Did that land on the proxy pool?

lia: Canary only, yes. Fallbacks should be fine but ingest seems to be rejecting session tickets / early data intermittently.

sam: Correlating with audit logs: KMS unwrap errors spike at same time: `kms:DecryptAccessDenied` for session keys. Could the keystore RBAC change be related?

noah: I rotated IAM roles last night — revoked a broad keystore role and created `ingest-kms-unwrap` with stricter conditions. Possible we missed tagging the proxy service account. Investigating now.

olivia: If KMS unwrap fails the runtime can't decrypt session resumption keys, so TLS resumption will fail and clients try full handshake. If cipher families mismatch it can lead to `no shared cipher`.

lia: Reproduction steps I ran: `curl --resolve ingest-eu.internal:443:10.2.3.7 https://ingest-eu.internal/health --tlsv1.3 -v` — intermittent `SSL3_GET_RECORD:wrong version number`. Stack attached in the incident doc.

deploy-bot: deployed canary proxy pool update: `proxy-config v2.14.1` to eu-canary at 2026-03-19T22:12:03Z

kms-bot: KMS log: DecryptRequest failed for key `projects/redwood/keys/ingest-session-key` — Principal `svc-proxy-eu@redwood.internal` : PermissionDenied (request=req-0a9f)

mike: Proposed plan: 1) roll back cipher-profile on eu-proxies to prior stable -> canary only 2) confirm KMS role tagging for svc-proxy-eu and fix IAM binding if missing 3) run e2e: `openssl s_client` + ingest health check 4) monitor audit logs and SLOs. Volunteers?

olivia: I'll run e2e and watch SLOs. Lia coordinate RBAC backfill with Noah. Sam can you push a temporary fallback to accept legacy session tickets: `session_ticket_allow_legacy: true` for canary?

sam: I can toggle flag for canary now and attach KMS request IDs for the period. Will do and report back (canary only).

noah: If we toggle, I'll enable audit detail: `audit.log.kms_unwrap=true` and retain logs 90d. Also creating an alert rule for `kms:DecryptAccessDenied` spike > 10/min.

lia: :thumbsup: Start canary toggle now. If canary stabilizes we roll forward after RBAC fix.

olivia: Tailing proxy + ingest logs. Toggle applied to eu-canary, session tickets accepted, ingest health -> 200/200 in canary after ~2m. KMS Unwrap errors dropped to 0 on canary.

kms-bot: Alert resolved for canary keys; alert id a-8721 auto-muted.

lia: Good. Rolling cipher-profile rollback + RBAC tag backfill to prod in 15m, then monitor. Adding follow-ups: RBAC verification in CI, audit rule, safe-deploy checklist update for cipher-profile changes.

sam: Opened ticket INC-2026-84 with owners and action items (RBAC CI job, KMS audit retention, must-gate for cipher-profile PRs).

olivia: Prod roll complete, SLOs back to normal, closing incident. Will add a short playbook for quick KMS unwrap smoke test to devkit.

lia: Postmortem planned: impact ~37m, root cause: RBAC keystore tag mismatch combined with aggressive canary cipher-profile change. Lessons: stricter RBAC needs service-account tagging verification + canary-only config flags should include KMS smoke checks.

auditbot: Postmortem ticket created: PM-SEC-2026-44 (links to INC-2026-84)

lia: Thanks everyone. Leaving final notes in incident page: https://wiki.redwood.internal/incidents/ingest-eu-tls-2524689012

olivia: Closing thread — will attach logs and timeline in the postmortem. :eyes:
